subject: Re: two observers, one of them measured in whole numbers

messages.author: 1919e0888c072eb3
messages.subject: two observers, one of them measured in whole numbers
parts:
dear mailing list!
i've encountered the following problem:
in order to prepare a publication on animal densities, a two observer
survey had been conducted in 2009. we were now trying to pool the
observations BUT... one of the observers measured distance in integers,
therefore I assume this dataset to be somewhat rounded. is there a way
to cope with that? i was thinking of adding generated random numbers to
each sample, constructed in a way that they will not alter median, mean,
sd, and variance of the samples, though I am quite sure this would not
be appropriate.
thanks in advance!

messages.author: 12f269733c6eb9a2
messages.subject: Re: two observers, one of them measured in whole numbers
parts:
Sacha:

The heaping you describe may or may not be an issue: if the truncation
distance is 1000m and distances are measured in metres, then heaping is
not worth concern. It would be of concern if the truncation distance is 5m.

You can employ appropriate cut-points for both observer's data (Buckland
et al. 2001:109) that reduce the influence of heaping by placing the
cut-points such that the 'correct' distance falls within the proper bin.

The remedy you suggest is a bit like 'smearing' (described in Buckland
et al (2001:269-271)) and available in Distance, but as you suggest it
is an ad hoc approach.
